question.text: Mr. Arjun Malhotra, a Mumbai-based tax counsel, is advising an AIF sponsor on the 'tax neutrality' principle in AIF pooling. Which of the following BEST describes tax neutrality as applied to AIF structures?

answer.text: Pooling eliminates all tax liabilities of investors arising from fund income
Pooling shifts tax incidence permanently from the investor to the Manager
Pooling guarantees a minimum post-tax return through use of tax treaties only
Pooling should not put an investor in a comparatively adverse tax position as compared to investing at individual level

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 8.2 item 3, tax neutrality means the investor should not end up worse-off post-tax through the pooled vehicle compared to investing directly. It is a design principle, not an elimination of tax or a guarantee of returns. The Trap: Option A exaggerates — pooling never eliminates tax. Option C confuses tax treaties with neutrality. Option D is wrong; incidence remains with the investor in a pass-through structure. Cross-Exam Context: XVI / XIX-C both cover Section 115UB pass-through for Cat I/II AIFs. Cat III AIFs do NOT enjoy full pass-through — so achieving neutrality is harder and is a recurring XIX-C question. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the tax disclosure section of the PPM, spell out the cases where pooling may create adverse outcomes (e.g., Cat III taxable at fund level). Transparency here prevents LP disputes later.
